supported_subtotals.assessment: The DC-copper-only deltas are all well below the 19.3765 W switching saving, leaving 12.63 W (760801202) / 16.00 W (760801403) / 14.43 W (760801321) of headroom for the unpublished AC winding + core loss before the saving is erased.

supported_subtotals.reason: Requires AC winding loss AND core loss at 65 kHz, 15 A rms bias, 4.2043 A pk-pk for both the candidate and the baseline. None of the four datasheets publishes either. The total is unknown, not the DC-only delta.

constraint_findings.finding: Baseline effective inductance at bias is below the value the frequency trade assumed
constraint_findings.detail: The retained model uses 180 uH as the 760800301 effective inductance. The datasheet's typical curve gives 159.8 uH at 23.2719 A (-11.2 % of nominal). The baseline's real ripple at its own L and 129 kHz would be ~4.74 A pk-pk rather than the supplied 4.2043 A. The supplied envelope was used unchanged for all loss numbers; only the loss values that depend on the baseline ripple are affected.

constraint_findings.finding: Printed ISAT and printed L-vs-bias curve disagree for two candidates
constraint_findings.detail: 760800301 and 760801202 agree with the family's |dL/L| < 30 % definition (digitized ratio 0.698 and 0.687 at the printed ISAT). 760801403 (0.957) and 760801321 (0.805) do not. For 760801403 the printed ISAT of 23 A is essentially the 23.2719 A envelope peak, so a conservative use of that part has NO saturation margin even though its curve looks flat.

constraint_findings.finding: Thermal envelope is conditional on forced air
constraint_findings.detail: The two L-matched parts (760801202 IR 11.5 A; 760801403 IR 12.3 A) are below the 15 A rms envelope at dT = 40 K without a fan; they pass only at the 4 m/s fan rating (IR2 20 A / 24.6 A). The only no-fan-capable member (760801321, IR 17.2 A) misses the inductance target by ~1.94x. Assembly airflow is not supplied, so thermal applicability is INDETERMINATE.

constraint_findings.finding: Core and AC winding loss are unpublished for every part, including the baseline
constraint_findings.detail: WE-TORPFC datasheets publish typical L vs current and typical temperature rise vs current only. There is no core-loss, Steinmetz, AC-resistance or impedance-vs-frequency data. Per the task rule, core loss is not inferred from DCR, so the magnetic term that decides the 19.38 W question stays null.

constraint_findings.finding: L tolerance is +/-20 % and the curve is typical only
constraint_findings.detail: A production unit at the -20 % tolerance edge would deliver ~280 uH at bias for the 760801202, raising ripple to ~5.25 A pk-pk and the peak to ~24.4 A. Whether that unit still passes ISAT is not established by this document.
None of the datasheets or the family page publishes a mass for any WE-TORPFC part; mass stays null for all candidates.

next_discriminating_observation: The single most important missing curve is the candidate choke's CORE LOSS (and AC winding resistance) at 65 kHz as a function of DC bias from 0 to 23.3 A, at 4.2043 A pk-pk ripple, for the 760801202 and the retained 760800301. This is the only remaining term that can consume the 19.3765 W switching saving. It is not published by Wurth; obtain it by requesting a core-loss/winding-loss measurement from the manufacturer for the exact bias/ripple/frequency, or measure both chokes on a B-H/calorimetric or impedance-analyzer bench at the envelope.

verdict_on_19_38_w.detail: DC-copper delta alone is +6.75 W (760801202) vs a 19.3765 W saving, so the saving is not erased by DC copper. But AC winding and core loss are unpublished for both the candidate and the baseline, so the full magnetic delta that the decision rule needs is unknown. A < 19.3765 W magnetic delta is plausible (14.43-16.00 W of DC-copper headroom remains) but is not established by these sources.
